purpose: Chlorzoxazone is used to help relieve pain and stiffness caused by muscle injuries, strains, or sprains. It is usually used along with rest and physical therapy to help you feel more comfortable while your muscles heal. It is meant for short-term use only.
how_it_works: Chlorzoxazone works by acting on your brain and spinal cord to reduce the muscle spasms that cause pain and tightness. Think of it as a signal blocker that tells your nervous system to calm down and let your muscles relax. It does not work directly on the muscle itself but through your central nervous system.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, lightheadedness, and upset stomach or nausea. You may also notice that your urine turns orange or reddish-purple in color — this is harmless and normal with this medication. Headache can also occur.
warnings: This medication can make you very drowsy, so do not drive or operate heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication as it can dangerously increase drowsiness. In rare cases, chlorzoxazone can cause serious liver problems — contact your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. Tell your doctor about all medications you take, especially other sedatives or sleep aids.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 500 mg taken three to four times a day. Your doctor may increase this to 750 mg three to four times a day if needed. It can be taken with food if it upsets your stomach. Always follow your doctor or pharmacist's specific instructions.
